“I’m not available for additional front-of-house shifts,” you say. “I want to keep the hours outside my archive contract for myself.”

Nell looks up from the rota.

“That’s fine. You aren’t on this list. I only mentioned it because it’s what I’ll be working on downstairs.”

She moves the availability sheets aside.

“Your contract is for archive work, thirty hours a week. The upstairs room is part of that contract; it doesn’t make you available for cover. I’ll treat this as a standing no to extra shifts.”

She does not ask you to justify it or suggest an exception for reopening weekend. Your name remains off the front-of-house rota.

Nell returns to matching the paid staff’s availability. The programme box and condition slips wait for you beside the office door.
